prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can I get a light French sparkling wine that tastes like cherry for under 15 euros? I don't drink fancy stuff, just something nice for every once in a while."

List A:
Wine 1: Sparkling Blend, Argentina, $8. Tasting note: "If you're looking for a pedestrian but true sparkling wine for under $10, this Chenin Blanc-based bubbly from Argentina is solid, a touch yeasty and dry. It tastes much like a Loire Valley sparkler, with baked apple, apricot and peach pit flavors. On the negative side, it's fairly foamy across the tongue and doesn't have a top-grade mouthfeel."
Wine 2: Sparkling Blend, US, $28. Tasting note: "Good price for a sparkling wine this delicious and refined. Offers lots of bubbly pleasure, with orange, lime, vanilla, honey and yeasty flavors. Made from Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc."
Wine 3: Sparkling Blend, France, $20. Tasting note: "A sweet sparkling wine that is fresh and clean, this comes from the south of France. The light, crisp character with some acidity leaves a fresh aftertaste. This is a new release from Barton & Gustier."
Wine 4: Chenin Blanc, France, $20. Tasting note: "One of the best sparkling wines to come from the Loire, this is a classically driven wine, packed with tingling acidity along with some toastiness and apple fruits. The wine is still fresh and could age a few more months in bottle."
Wine 5: Sparkling Blend, US, $25. Tasting note: "Excellent price for a coastal sparkling wine made from the superior grape varieties of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. Rich and ripe in strawberries, limes and vanilla, it has a doughy yeastiness, with crisp acidity and a dry finish."

List B:
Wine 1: Sparkling Blend, Argentina, $8. Tasting note: "If you're looking for a pedestrian but true sparkling wine for under $10, this Chenin Blanc-based bubbly from Argentina is solid, a touch yeasty and dry. It tastes much like a Loire Valley sparkler, with baked apple, apricot and peach pit flavors. On the negative side, it's fairly foamy across the tongue and doesn't have a top-grade mouthfeel."
Wine 2: Sparkling Blend, US, $75. Tasting note: "Complex and well balanced, this elegant dry, barrel-fermented sparkling wine has light white-cherry aromas, crisp fruit flavors with a touch of buttery richness, and a tangy, citrus finish. Quite dry and classic in style, it will get more interesting with age; it will be best to drink after 2019."
Wine 3: Cabernet Franc, US, $20. Tasting note: "A very easy wine to like. It's so softly balanced, so rich in cherries, licorice and smoky vanilla, so light in texture, you could drink it as a cocktail wine. But it will also nicely complement a wide variety of foods."
Wine 4: Portuguese Sparkling, Portugal, $12. Tasting note: "This off-dry sparkling wine has ripe cherry fruits as well as a touch of tannin for texture. It is crisp, clean, delicately fruity, and ready to drink at any time."
Wine 5: Merlot, US, $15. Tasting note: "A nice Bordeaux style wine for fifteen bucks. It's dry and firmly tannic, with black currant and cola flavors, and some elegance. Fine now with a steak or chop."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
